entries.title: Kottu roti
entries.body: Final supper type food. Nothing else to say really. Chopped good shit.

entries.title: Hoppers (with or without egg)
entries.body: Similar to a pancake batter, it's quite crispy and you have it with a chilli sambal. So nice.

entries.title: String hoppers
entries.body: Noodle nest ting.

entries.title: Pol roti
entries.body: Coconut flatbread with lunu miris (spicy onion chilli sambal). Simple but slaps.

entries.title: Rice and curry
entries.body: Yo you gotta eat with your hands tho.

entries.title: Short eats
entries.body: Short eats is the name for any snack you see on the way to somewhere. They're sweet or savoury and they're stunning. Loads of veggie options too. The best veggie ones are:
list: Elawolu roti (roti parcels of flavoured potato and veggies)
Bithara roti (same but with egg for the prote)
Rolls (veg and potato mix, wrapped in a thin pancake, dipped in golden breadcrumbs and fried. Unreal.)
Cutlets (same, minus the pancake, and small balls)
entries.after: Honestly so many of these I can't list them all, but you'll see them.

entries.title: Anything devilled
entries.body: It just means fried and tossed in what is basically a sweet and sour sauce, but with more flavour and much nicer.

entries.title: Sri Lankan fried rice
entries.body: Slightly different to regular fried rice but not hugely.

entries.title: Seafood
entries.body: Crab curry, prawn curry, fish curry all bangers.

entries.title: Jaffna crab curry
entries.body: Northern speciality, properly spicy. Wear a bib.

sections.label: Fruit

entries.title: Jackfruit
entries.body: Try it before you knock it. Ik there's cooked jackfruit here in burgers and stuff but it's unbelievably better when it's ripe.

entries.title: Rambutan (South Asian version of lychee)
entries.body: Lush.

entries.title: Mangosteen
entries.body: My fave Sri Lankan fruit. Kinda messy to eat but please have one, they're the GOAT.

entries.title: Mango
entries.body: >>>> Tesco mangos. You can also get raw mango mixed with chilli and salt at the roadside stalls. V common snack.

entries.title: Guava
entries.body: There's white or pink guava, try both. The pink ones are much sweeter than the white ones.

entries.title: King coconut (orange coconut)
entries.body: The coconut water is a popular drink and these ones are deffo safe from the roadside (cause the shell, obvs). One hack: when you finish it, ask them to crack it open. There's loads of really soft, sweet coconut flesh inside which you can eat and it is lush. They even make you a little spoon out of coconut shell to eat it with.

entries.title: Durian
entries.body: Stinky. Not for me. Might be for y'all.

entries.title: Bananas
entries.body: 29 types of banana?! Collect them all.

entries.title: Wood apple (divul)
entries.body: Banging juice fruit.

entries.title: Soursop (anoda)
entries.body: Top 3 fruits of all time.

entries.title: Rose apple (jambu)
entries.body: Mid tbh, like a crunchy water balloon.

entries.title: Pineapple
entries.body: Not sad supermarket ones.

sections.intro: Best place to get fruit, in my opinion, is the roadside stalls. They're literally everywhere and, depending on who you talk to, they may or may not be clean? But also, when in Rome. It's delish, but eat at your own risk.

entries.title: Buffalo curd with kitul pani
entries.body: Not really a dessert, but they always sell buffalo curd on the side of the road, which I personally love, and it slaps with kitul pani, which is like maple syrup but made from palm trees.

entries.title: Wattalapan
entries.body: Basically a crème brûlée but made with coconut milk.

entries.title: Dodol
entries.body: I don't love it but a lot of people do. Like a gelatinous fudge?

entries.title: Helapa
entries.body: I like this but a lot of people don't, ahah. Sweet dough wrapped in banana leaf (the leaf is for steaming, don't eat it).

entries.title: Bibikkan
entries.body: Coconut cake.

entries.title: Kiri toffee
entries.body: Fudge but with coconut milk.

entries.title: The palm sugar pancake one
entries.body: Don't know what they're called but palm sugar n coconut all wrapped up in a pancake. You'll know if you see it ;)

entries.title: Kokis
entries.body: I'm not the biggest fan, kinda just deep fried batter. Vessel for oil.

entries.title: Pani walalu
entries.body: Wayyy too sweet imo.

entries.title: Hikkaduwa beach
entries.body: Very nice area, good seafood places, good for snorkelling (can hire the gear on the beach) and sometimes have turtles hatching in local sanctuaries.

entries.title: Arugam Bay beach
entries.body: Famous for the waves and surfing. Stunning beach, quite touristy, loads of cool, edgy Sri Lankan surf dudes that will surf with you. Very hot.

entries.title: Trincomalee beaches
entries.body: Beware tiny jellyfish.

entries.title: Pigeon Island
entries.body: This is THEE spot for snorkelling, nice coral reefs and sometimes have blacktip reef sharks you can swim with. Haven't got bitten so far so I think it's safe. Gotta hire a boat to get there but that's cheaps and often.
Light, breathable clothes: it is hot and humid on the coast and in the Cultural Triangle.
One warm layer: hill country nights (Nuwara Eliya, Ella) get cold.
Rain jacket or small umbrella: December is wet season in the north and east.
Temple outfit: something that covers shoulders and knees, plus shoes you can slip off (you go barefoot inside).
Swimwear, and a quick-dry towel.
Sunscreen, hat and sunglasses.
Insect repellent (mosquitoes at dusk).
Plug adapter: Sri Lanka uses type D and type G sockets, 230 V.
Power bank for long drives and train days.
Basic meds: rehydration salts, anti-diarrhoea tablets, antihistamines, plasters.
Hand sanitiser and tissues (not every toilet has paper).
Comfy shoes with grip for Pidurangala and Ella Rock.
Small dry bag for boat trips and rafting.
Day pack.
Some cash in rupees (LKR) for roadside stalls and tuk-tuks; cards work in most hotels and bigger restaurants.
Copies of your passport and travel authorisation, saved on your phone.
